title: Strategy Leadership Lab
text:
Content Overview
Strategy Leadership Lab is a weekly working session for the roughly 30 students who lead the BYU Strategy Program and its four clubs: MCA, PMA, CSA, and WSA. It exists to do two things at once: develop you as a leader, and give the whole leadership team protected time to coordinate on shared priorities.
The Lab is the primary coordination mechanism in the Strategy Program operating model. One meeting cadence governs the entire program.
Enrollment is limited to program and club leaders. It is optional but encouraged for everyone serving in a presidency. If your schedule prevents you from enrolling, you are welcome to audit or simply attend.

title: Strategy Leadership Lab
text:
Credit and Pay
Students do not receive pay and credit for the same work.

Class is where you reflect, discuss, and learn. The job is where you execute, deliver, and coordinate.
Student employees may not log paid work hours during scheduled class sessions or on class-specific assignments.

title: Operating Model
text:
Strategy Program Operating Model
The Strategy Program has grown by 50% over the last five years and now serves 120 new students per year. The operating model below aligns faculty, student leaders, career services, and academic advisement at that scale. It has three parts.

Timeline. Most positions are filled in March and active by May. MCA is the exception: co-presidents are selected in November, after consulting offers settle. Off-cycle graduations can create mid-year vacancies, which the relevant hiring committee fills as needed.
MCA co-president criteria: demonstrated success in consulting recruiting, leadership ability, and credibility to represent the program to top firms.
